title: Meet Petit Verdot
subtitle: Small berries, deep colour
objectives: Describe Petit Verdot's colour and flavours

steps.title: A dark spice
steps.body: Petit Verdot is a black grape from Bordeaux. Its small, thick-skinned berries give very deep colour, high tannin and high acidity. It smells of violet, blackberry, blueberry, and spices like clove and sage. In a blend, a few percent is enough to add colour, structure and a floral, spicy lift.

steps.title: Why little green
steps.body: Its name means little green one, because in Bordeaux it often failed to ripen fully. It buds early and ripens very late, often after Cabernet Sauvignon. In cool years, it stayed green and harsh. That's why Bordeaux planted little of it, and used it only as a seasoning in the blend.

steps.explanation: It means little green one, because in Bordeaux it often stayed unripe.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: In a Bordeaux blend, you may not notice Petit Verdot directly, but it deepens the colour and adds a violet and spice note, and firmer tannin on the finish. Alone, it is inky purple, intense, with violets and dark fruit, firm tannin and fresh acidity.

steps.prompt: What does Petit Verdot add to a blend?
steps.explanation: Petit Verdot adds acidity, not lowers it.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Petit Verdot gives deep colour, tannin, acidity and spice
Its name means little green one, from struggling to ripen
It seasons Bordeaux blends and can stand alone
